# windows_os_info (Data Source)

Reads the OS inventory of the remote Windows host without managing it. This is a **singleton** data source — no lookup keys are required.

Exposes `product_name`, `version`, `build_number` / `ubr` (combined as `full_build`), `display_version`, `edition_id`, the numeric `sku` with its `sku_name`, `installation_type`, `is_server` / `is_server_core`, `product_type`, `architecture`, `install_date`, `last_boot_time`, `system_drive`, `windows_directory`, `os_language`, `powershell_version`, and the stable machine ID (HKLM MachineGuid), exposed as the resource `id`.

The Terraform data source ID is the stable machine ID (HKLM MachineGuid).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Singleton — no lookup keys required.
data "windows_os_info" "current" {}

output "product_name" {
  value = data.windows_os_info.current.product_name
}

output "full_build" {
  value = data.windows_os_info.current.full_build
}

# Example: only manage a resource on Server Core hosts.
resource "terraform_data" "core_only" {
  count = data.windows_os_info.current.is_server_core ? 1 : 0
}

# Requires Terraform 1.5+ for check blocks.
check "supported_os" {
  assert {
    condition     = contains(["ServerStandard", "ServerDatacenter"], data.windows_os_info.current.edition_id)
    error_message = "Unsupported OS edition: ${data.windows_os_info.current.edition_id}."
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `architecture` (String) Processor architecture name: x86, arm, x64 or arm64; empty when unknown.
- `build_number` (Number) OS build (HKLM CurrentVersion CurrentBuild).
- `display_version` (String) Friendly version (CurrentVersion DisplayVersion, ReleaseId on older hosts).
- `edition_id` (String) OS edition (CurrentVersion EditionID).
- `full_build` (String) Build number, or build.ubr when UBR is greater than zero.
- `id` (String) Data source ID; the stable machine ID (HKLM MachineGuid).
- `install_date` (String) OS install time in UTC RFC 3339; empty when unavailable.
- `installation_type` (String) Installation type (CurrentVersion InstallationType).
- `is_server` (Boolean) True when the product type is DomainController or Server; false otherwise, including unknown values.
- `is_server_core` (Boolean) True when the installation type is Server Core.
- `last_boot_time` (String) Last boot time in UTC RFC 3339; empty when unavailable.
- `os_language` (String) OS culture name; empty when unavailable.
- `powershell_version` (String) Responding PowerShell engine version.
- `product_name` (String) OS caption (Win32_OperatingSystem.Caption).
- `product_type` (String) Product type name: Workstation, DomainController or Server; empty when unknown.
- `sku` (Number) Numeric OS SKU (Win32_OperatingSystem.OperatingSystemSKU).
- `sku_name` (String) SKU mapped to its documented product name; empty when unknown.
- `system_drive` (String) System drive (Win32_OperatingSystem.SystemDrive).
- `ubr` (Number) Update build revision (HKLM CurrentVersion UBR).
- `version` (String) OS version (Win32_OperatingSystem.Version).
- `windows_directory` (String) Windows directory (Win32_OperatingSystem.WindowsDirectory).

### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
